Done
say if user exists with same name, then "err" set to true and then there is no point to proceed to line number 640 to 654 since we can't proceed rename right?

in the `err = true` case, `isUserExistSystem(newUserName)` is true which means that one of two things happened - maybe there was some race and the newUserName was created after `throwForUserExists(newUserName)` but before `executeUserRename`

or alternatively, the rename was just partly successful. like `usermod` may have just failed to rename a home dir or something (we can dig through the usermod source to see what failure modes it has).

in the second case, we should definitely run lines 640 through 654 so that the in-memory state reflects what's on the system (new user ends up existing, old user is removed)

do you know if phosphor-user-manager can have the race condition described above where it simultaneously handles both a create and rename? I hadn't considered that before, but could add logic to check if both the old and new users exist, in which case I'd agree with skipping 640 to 654, or at minimum adding the new user to the in-memory struct if it's missing so that a future call tracks both users as present.

yeah we can dig more on usermod failures.
I dont think user-manager have race condition simultaneously handling both a create and rename at the same time.
I think we can merge this patch and address this rework in future commits
